claim_verdicts.evidence: State page: "This state is stored by default in a local file named \"terraform.tfstate\""; "used by OpenTofu to map real world resources to your configuration". Local backend: path defaults to "terraform.tfstate" relative to the root module. Sensitive-data: "When using local state, state is stored in plain-text JSON files." Encryption: "OpenTofu supports encrypting state and plan files at rest" - the ledger's no-encryption condition matches lesson sec. 3 ("in `first-cluster` it is a plain-text file").

Resource addressing: address is "[module path][resource spec]", resource spec "resource_type.resource_name[instance index]". Round 2: lesson sec. 3 now scopes the type.name form to "a resource in the configuration's own folder", matching the ledger. Captured run: "$ tofu state list" / "kind_cluster.this".

Variables page: `sensitive` "prevents OpenTofu from showing its value in the `plan` or `apply` output"; "OpenTofu will still record sensitive values in the state". References page: "When defining the schema for a resource type, a provider developer can mark certain attributes as sensitive"; OpenTofu will "show a placeholder marker `(sensitive value)`". Lesson sec. 3 (new) gives `sensitive = true` as the way a value "becomes one", omitting provider-marked attributes.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Sensitive value — a value OpenTofu hides in what plan and apply print, showing `(sensitive value)` in its place; the configuration can mark one with `sensitive = true`, and a provider can mark some of a resource's attributes sensitive itself.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Plan: by default "Reads the current state of any already-existing remote objects", "Compares the current configuration to the prior state". Resource behavior: "Create resources that exist in the configuration but are not associated with a real infrastructure object in the state"; "Destroy resources that exist in the state but no longer exist in the configuration" (a `removed` block makes it forget instead). Round 2: lesson sec. 4 now says "with nothing in the files about it any more".

issues.text: New in round 2: the Sensitive value definition names `sensitive = true` in the configuration as how a value becomes sensitive. OpenTofu references docs: "a provider developer can mark certain attributes as sensitive" in the resource schema, and plans then show "(sensitive value)". A learner may conclude an attribute nobody marked, such as `client_key`, cannot be sensitive.
